newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end off as NAPM shatters early gains.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end off as NAPM shatters early gains.

text.p: The Dutch AEX share index ended down 2.59 points at 980.74 on Friday, mirroring the Dow's drop which was triggered by the release of the July NAPM index.

Boosted by strong gains in index heavyweights, the index had spent most of the day at higher levels, but slipped at the end of the session when a 58.6 July NAPM index -- well above forecasts -- sent bonds and stocks tumbling.
Earlier, U.S. employment data for July had caused price volatility, but ended up supporting the market.

Non-farm payrolls showed a rise of 316,000 in July, above the 193,000 expected and up from the revised 228,000 rise in June, but unchanged average hourly earnings of $12.23 and a drop in average weekly hours comforted market players.
"The employment data had good and bad sides, but the overall outcome was positive for the market," one dealer said.
Shares in index heavyweight Unilever ended up 12.40 guilders at 467.40 after the food and detergents group announced a 4-for-1 stock split before bourse opening.
The company announced a net profit at current exchange rates of 9.21 billion guilders versus 1.75 billion a year earlier.
Excluding profits from the sale of its specialty chemicals business, net profit at current exchange rates came to 2.38 billion guilders, still outstripping market expectations.
"A stock-split seems to be a guarantee for a 10 guilders rise," one dealer said, adding the results were fine but that Unilever had been very cautious about its prospects.
Chemicals group Akzo added another 19.70 to close at 340.50, having already risen 18.30 guilders on Thursday following well-received second quarter results.
Dealers said the stock was also boosted by an upgrade to a "buy" rating by investment bank CSFB.
Optical discs acquipment maker Toolex Alpha rose eight percent to 22.20 guilders in busy trade, pulling with it Axxicon and Docdata.
Some dealers linked the rise to news U.S. FMR corp had taken a 7.4 percent stake in Toolex. Axxicon added six percent to end at 29.50 guilders, Docdata closed up 1.50 guilders at 33.50.
Hoogovens, due to release second quarter results on Wednesday next week, ended up 9.30 guilders at 134.80.
"Expectations for Hoogovens' results, due on Wednesday, are quite high. It's a cyclical company and once those get started, things can go fast," one dealer said.
